Synopsis:
Before the point of no return when about to fight the brain, the player encounters Voss. If Orpheus is alive, he says he will help the player in combat. if Orpheus is dead, what happens depends on whether he is an illithid or not,

Cluster Contexts:
- END_VossEncounter_VossAmbush.json: The scene takes place just before the "point of no return"—the final approach to fight the Netherbrain—when the player runs into Kith'rak Voss, a furious Githyanki who served Prince Orpheus. If Orpheus survived, Voss will ally with and help the player in the upcoming combat. If Orpheus is dead, Voss is hostile, accuses the player of murdering the heir and even calls them an “illithid” (mind flayer), blaming them for dooming his people. Lae'zel may interject to explain that Orpheus’s death was a necessary sacrifice to stop the Grand Design, but tensions remain high and combat or threats are likely.
- END_IllithidOptions_OrpheusFreed.json: Orpheus is now freed from the player's assistance. They now have the option to take the Mind Flayer form, or to give Orpheus that responsibility. He is not really impressed with the tadpole in the player's head. It's possible the player would have fought Orpheus in Intermezzo before this point, so there should be some reactivity to it.
- INT_EmperorRevealed_AfterOrpheus.json: With Orpheus subdued, players learn of the true nature of Daisy, some of the Emperor's backstory, the technicality of how Orpheus' power protects them, and the scale of what they are up against when it comes to the Brain's intelligence. They might transform into a half-illithid.
- END_IllithidOptions_PAD_OutOfOptions.json: Player has rejected Emperor and doesn't have the means to free Orpheus, but knows that in order to defeat the Netherbrain they need to a) be illithid to wield the stones to their full effect, and b) assimilate Orpheus' power. If the player has the supreme tadpole, they can still assimilate Orpheus.
- INT_EmperorRevealed_EmperorPlea.json: The Emperor tries to get you to help it destroy Orpheus' royal guard so that it can subdue Orpheus again. If you side with the Emperor, you fight against the githyanki with the help of the Emperor and the intellect devourers. If you side with the githyanki, the Emperor feels betrayed and will teleport you back to the material plane where you have a few turns to get back inside the portal and some githyanki to kill on your way.

If Orpheus is dead, Voss is hostile, accuses the player of murdering the heir and even calls them an “illithid” (mind flayer), blaming them for dooming his people. He is not really impressed with the tadpole in the player's head. It's possible the player would have fought Orpheus in Intermezzo before this point, so there should be some reactivity to it.

If the player has the supreme tadpole, they can still assimilate Orpheus.

context: You meet Kith'rak Voss—an enraged Githyanki who served Prince Orpheus—just before the point of no return as you approach the Netherbrain. If Orpheus is alive and recognized as heir, Voss will ally with and help you in the coming fight; if Orpheus is dead Voss is hostile, accuses you of murdering the heir, and even calls you an "illithid," blaming you for dooming his people. Lae'zel may try to defuse him by arguing Orpheus' death was a necessary sacrifice to stop the Grand Design, but tensions are high and violence or threats are likely. How Voss reacts also depends on Orpheus' present condition (freed, transformed into an illithid, or otherwise), and on whether the player appears connected to illithid power.
